title: Standard Input, Standard Output, and Standard Error
keywords: Standard Input, Standard Output, and Standard Error
learning_outcomes: Describe stdin and explain how it relates to Standard Input, Standard Output, and Standard Error.
Demonstrate stdout in a small Node.js example and predict the observable result.
Test a failure, boundary, lifecycle, or version-compatibility case involving stderr.

content.intro: Standard Input, Standard Output, and Standard Error is part of javascript execution inside nodejs. This lesson connects stdin, stdout, stderr to a concrete Node.js example. Focus on the behavior you can observe, the assumptions the API makes, and one failure or boundary case.
content.why_it_matters: Streams process data in chunks so an application can handle large or continuous input without buffering it all at once. Test empty input, stream errors, a deliberately slow consumer, and memory usage with representative files.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Streams process data in chunks so an application can handle large or continuous input without buffering it all at once. Compose streams with pipeline-style error handling and respect backpressure from slow consumers.

items.title: Basic stream-based terminal interaction
items.text: Streams process data incrementally. Backpressure allows a slow consumer to regulate a faster producer instead of accumulating unbounded memory.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety note
content_blocks.text: Teaching baseline: use a supported Node.js LTS release (Node.js 24 LTS as checked on 2026-10-13). The official releases page lists Node.js 26 as Current and Node.js 24/22 as LTS. Some advanced APIs, flags, permission behavior, embedded SQLite capabilities, module-loader hooks, and TypeScript integration are version-sensitive; verify the exact installed runtime. The Node.js 22 runtime available in the build-check environment is used only for syntax checks. This example is for learning and static validation, not for executing untrusted learner code inside CodeLeaf.

content.task: Create or inspect a small Node.js example for Standard Input, Standard Output, and Standard Error. Include at least one listed subtopic, document the expected result, and verify a normal case plus a boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates a named lesson concept, rather than only mentioning the title.
Expected output or observable behavior is documented and reproducible.
At least one invalid, empty, timeout, resource, or failure case is handled or explained.
The solution does not put secrets in source code and does not execute untrusted code inside the production API process.
hints: Start with stdin; identify the input, operation, and observable result.
Run the smallest relevant example in the selected Node.js release before adding frameworks or external services.
Test one failure or boundary case for stdout, then explain why the outcome is expected.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring write() backpressure or failing to propagate stream errors and cleanup.
common_mistakes.why: The code may pass a simple demonstration yet fail with real inputs, resource limits, timing, or runtime differences.
common_mistakes.fix: Use pipeline() where suitable and pause/retry writes when the writable stream signals backpressure.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its runtime, dependencies, input assumptions, or cleanup behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Node.js APIs and surrounding ecosystem tools have explicit version, trust, and resource boundaries.
common_mistakes.fix: State the environment and dependency assumptions, then rerun the example from a clean starting state.
